long_biography.plain_text:
Bode Miller grew up near Franconia, New Hampshire, in an off-grid home and learned to ski at nearby Cannon Mountain. A scholarship to Carrabassett Valley Academy brought formal race training. His unconventional technique and willingness to improvise at speed became trademarks as he rose through the United States team and made his Olympic debut in 1998.

Miller became the first American man to win World Cup races in all five alpine disciplines. Across five Olympics he collected six medals, including combined gold in Vancouver, while two overall World Cup titles confirmed his range across technical and speed events. After retiring in 2017, he applied that experience to ski design and sports businesses, worked as a television analyst and supported youth and adaptive sport through the Turtle Ridge Foundation.
